title: arXiv physics — weekly notable papers (25 Sep–2 Oct 2026)
global_caveat: This is an inferred notable-paper selection, not an official arXiv trending chart or a most-read/downloaded ranking. The papers are too new for useful citation momentum, and the date-filtered bulk API query was rate-limited; archive listing checks and selected abstract/full-text verification were used instead.

sections.title: Interpreting the High-Recoil LUX-ZEPLIN Event with Bino-/Singlino-like and Higgsino Dark Matter
sections.abstract: The authors study elastic and inelastic supersymmetric dark-matter models that could produce LZ's reported approximately 248-keV recoil candidate, and show that the models predict different recoil spectra.
sections.claimed_result: The paper presents viable elastic bino/singlino-like and endothermic pseudo-Dirac Higgsino benchmarks and argues their recoil spectra differ away from the candidate.
sections.evidence_type: Theoretical; supersymmetric model calculations and recoil-spectrum comparisons against the LZ event context.
sections.unique_caveat: LZ's candidate has only 2.6σ global significance after the look-elsewhere effect, so it is not evidence of a dark-matter detection. The interpretation is model-dependent and uses approximations for detector response and halo/nuclear inputs.

sections.title: Is DESI Seeing Dynamical Dark Energy, or a Cosmic Glitch in Gravity?
sections.abstract: Combining DESI DR2 baryon acoustic oscillations with CMB datasets, the authors report a 3.3σ preference for a one-parameter reduction in cosmological gravitational coupling relative to Newton's constant, which fits at least as well as a two-parameter evolving-dark-energy model.
sections.claimed_result: The authors infer G_cosmo/G_N = 0.9920 ± 0.0025 from CMB+DESI and report that the preference remains about 3.3σ with the additional lensing and supernova datasets.
sections.evidence_type: Observational-data analysis; DESI DR2 BAO, Planck-PR4, ACT DR6, SPT-3G, optional CMB lensing and DES supernova data, interpreted using modified-CAMB/PPF calculations.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a model-dependent statistical preference, not a discovery of modified gravity; the authors use a phenomenological perturbation prescription and note limitations of the effective-fluid representation.

sections.title: First double-differential cross-section measurements in proton multiplicity and kinematics for mesonless νμ charged-current interactions on argon using the MicroBooNE detector
sections.abstract: MicroBooNE reports first double-differential measurements of muon-neutrino charged-current interactions on argon with no mesons and at least one proton, using proton multiplicity and kinematics in its full Booster Neutrino Beam dataset.
sections.claimed_result: The collaboration reports that the measurements are sensitive to final-state-interaction modeling and that none of the tested event generators fully describes the data, with mismatches in proton multiplicity and subleading-proton distributions.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; the full MicroBooNE Booster Neutrino Beam sample, corresponding to 1.30×10^21 protons on target, analyzed with detector-response corrections and compared with event-generator predictions.
sections.unique_caveat: The disagreement is a model/data comparison in one experiment and one beam/detector configuration; it does not by itself identify which nuclear-interaction mechanism is missing.

sections.title: Improved Constraints on Cosmic Microwave Background Circular Polarization with CLASS
sections.abstract: Using CLASS measurements at 90, 150, and 220 GHz alongside its earlier 40-GHz data, the team tightens large-scale CMB circular-polarization limits by about a factor of five and reports first limits on the temperature–circular-polarization power spectrum.
sections.claimed_result: The authors find both VV and TV spectra consistent with zero and give 95%-confidence upper limits, including 5.4×10^-3 μK_CMB^2 for large-scale VV and 5.8×10^-1 μK_CMB^2 for TV at 30<ℓ<50.
sections.evidence_type: Observational; CLASS data at 40, 90, 150, and 220 GHz, with Planck temperature data for the TV constraint.
sections.unique_caveat: These are upper limits rather than a detection; separating a cosmological circular-polarization signal from atmospheric contributions remains central to interpretation.

sections.title: Quantization through Dissipation and the Optical Quantum Hall Effect
sections.abstract: The authors combine terahertz Faraday-rotation measurements and numerical analysis to argue that a faint, low-frequency dissipative contribution from impurity states is needed to recover quantized Hall plateaus from the optical response.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report that the cyclotron resonance alone does not yield quantized plateaus under Kramers–Kronig transformation; including the weak low-frequency, topologically enforced dissipative component restores quantization.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental and computational; high-precision terahertz Faraday rotation, supported by numerical analysis.
sections.unique_caveat: The proposed mechanism relies on resolving a faint low-frequency impurity-state contribution; its quantitative robustness across samples and disorder conditions remains to be established.

sections.title: When Streams Curve Away: a Test of Dark Matter from Extragalactic Stellar Stream Populations
sections.abstract: The authors propose a geometry-only statistic of projected stellar-stream tracks to infer halo-shape populations and forecast that future large stream catalogs could distinguish collisionless CDM from self-interacting dark matter.
sections.claimed_result: A projected stream segment curving away from its host center is proposed as a simple diagnostic; the rate of such convex segments is predicted to depend on halo triaxiality and thus dark-matter model.
sections.evidence_type: Theoretical and computational forecast; geometric diagnostic and forecast for future survey-scale stream catalogs.
sections.unique_caveat: The stated significance is a forecast, not a present detection or constraint; its value depends on future catalog size, selection effects, and calibration of the relation between stream shapes and halo populations.
